heard: A new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1% chance of hitting Earth. On December 27, 2024, the Atlas Telescope in Chile spotted asteroid 2024 YR-4 sneaking past a solar blind spot. This city killer reached level 3 on the Torino scale, the highest impact hazard ever measured for its size. Roughly 53 to 67 meters wide, it packed the explosive punch of 8 megatons of TNT. A potential impact corridor, stretched across Nigeria and South America, threatening millions for several weeks. Many feared a December 22, 2032 collision, with an energy equivalent to 500 Hiroshima bombs. Refined data cleared Earth, shifted the danger briefly to the Moon, and finally cleared both. Now, astronomers only remember the panic from when a new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1% chance of hitting Earth. You
